source_name: Odessa Journal / Silicon Canals / Sesamers — English secondary coverage of Ukrainian fintech funding
why_relevant: Second-tier English outlets that pick up Ukrainian fintech funding and valuation events (Fintech-IT Group / mono ecosystem unicorn round backed by the Ukraine-Moldova American Enterprise Fund, ~EUR 16.5m raise). Individually low-authority but collectively they fill gaps where Finextra and The Paypers do not run the item, and they often quote the vendor's own PR verbatim.

source_name: PCI SSC — Qualified Security Assessor (QSA) company directory
why_relevant: Authoritative global listing of QSA companies filterable by market served; the canonical way to enumerate which assessor firms are entitled to audit Ukrainian banks, PSPs and processors, and which local firms hold QSA status.

source_name: PCI SSC — Approved Scanning Vendor (ASV) / PIN / P2PE / 3DS assessor listings
why_relevant: Beyond QSA, the ASV, PCI PIN, P2PE and 3DS assessor and validated-product listings expose which security firms and which certified hardware/software components (HSMs, PIN entry devices, P2PE solutions) are in scope for Ukrainian acquirers and processors.

source_name: Compliance Control — PCI QSA firm (Ukraine/CIS)
why_relevant: PCI SSC-accredited QSA operating in Ukraine, self-described as one of the earliest specialised PCI DSS certification firms in the region; its service pages, case references and client logos reveal which Ukrainian banks/PSPs it assesses.

source_name: Allcontrols — PCI DSS audit/consulting firm (Ukraine)
why_relevant: Ukrainian firm claiming PCI SSC accreditation and QSA status; a direct competitor/partner node in the compliance-services layer and a source of named client and scope references.

source_name: ESKA Global — Ukrainian cybersecurity firm, PCI DSS preparation practice
why_relevant: Local security consultancy publishing PCI DSS practitioner content; blog and case pages often name banks, processors and the tooling deployed, exposing vendor presence not visible in marketing channels.

source_name: SOCSERVE (soc.ua) — PCI DSS v4.0.1 assessment support, Ukraine
why_relevant: Ukrainian SOC/compliance provider; pages describe PCI DSS v4.x scope work and by extension the security stack (SIEM, scanning, WAF) it deploys for financial clients.

source_name: H-X Technologies — КСЗІ implementation and cybersecurity audit (Ukraine)
why_relevant: Local firm specialising in КСЗІ (state comprehensive information protection system) build and state expertise — the Ukraine-specific assurance regime that sits alongside PCI DSS for banks and payment infrastructure; its content names the certified protection products used.

source_name: ТЗІ Україна — organisation of state expertise of КСЗІ
why_relevant: Explains the КСЗІ state-expertise process and the role of 'суб'єкти оцінювання' (evaluation subjects) listed by Держспецзв'язку — a pointer into the Ukrainian licensed-assessor population that audits bank and payment-system information systems.

source_name: CSIRT-NBU — NBU banking-sector cyber incident response team portal
why_relevant: The central bank's own cyber defence centre for the banking system; publishes advisories, threat information and interaction rules with banks. Advisories periodically name affected software/products, revealing what is actually deployed in Ukrainian banks.

source_name: CERT-UA — government CERT advisories and recommendations
why_relevant: State CERT under Держспецзв'язку; its numbered advisories describe attacks on financial institutions and routinely name specific software, remote-access tools and infrastructure observed on victim networks — an independent evidence path to vendor presence.

source_name: NBU legal acts — cyber protection and information security regulation for banks (Postanova 178, 4, 24 and drafts)
why_relevant: The NBU's Provision on organisation of cyber protection in the banking system sets requirements for independent information-security audit of banks, CSIRT-NBU information exchange and protection of critical information infrastructure — it defines who may audit banks and therefore which assurance firms can sell into the sector.

source_name: NBU Resolution No. 143 — information security requirements for non-bank financial institutions
why_relevant: Vendor/consultancy explainers of Postanova 143 map the control set non-bank payment institutions must implement by the compliance deadline — an early indicator of procurement demand and of which suppliers are positioning against each control.

source_name: Держспецзв'язку (cip.gov.ua) — independent information-security audit of critical infrastructure: auditor requirements and register
why_relevant: Defines attestation requirements for information-security auditors and maintains a Перелік (register) of attested auditors entitled to audit critical infrastructure operators, which includes banks and payment infrastructure — a named-entity list of the assurance supplier population.

source_name: Cabinet of Ministers — resolution on independent information-security audit of critical infrastructure
why_relevant: Primary legal basis for the audit cadence (every 2–3 years by criticality category) and auditor qualification rules; sets the recurring demand cycle that assurance vendors sell into.

source_name: NAAU — National Accreditation Agency of Ukraine, register of accredited testing laboratories and certification bodies
why_relevant: Publishes the register of ISO/IEC 17025 testing laboratories and 17021/17065 certification bodies in Ukraine — the route to identifying labs that could test terminal/POS hardware and bodies certifying ISMS for financial institutions.

source_name: УкрКарт (UkrCard) — ПРОСТІР processing centre, card/terminal certification news
why_relevant: Operator/processor for the national ПРОСТІР scheme; its press releases document contactless EMV CPA chip card testing, terminal onboarding and member-bank counts — direct evidence of which terminal and card products are certified for the domestic scheme.

source_name: ProCard (Прокард) — Ukrainian processing centre, PCI DSS / PCI PIN / PCI 3DS audit disclosures
why_relevant: Processor that states it undergoes PCI DSS, PCI PIN Security and PCI 3DS audits on a regular basis; certification pages and news identify its assessor, standard versions and certified scope — a template for tracking every Ukrainian processor's assurance posture.

source_name: Ukrainian Processing Center (UPC) — corporate/certification pages
why_relevant: The largest independent Ukrainian card processor; its compliance and partner pages reveal certified platforms, ATM/POS driver support and the security standards it maintains for bank clients.

source_name: Bank PCI DSS compliance disclosure pages (e.g. Ukreximbank 'Міжнародний сертифікат PCI DSS Compliance')
why_relevant: Banks publish their own PCI DSS certification statements, sometimes naming the assessor and certified scope; systematically harvesting these across Ukrainian banks builds a compliance-driven vendor/assessor map.

source_name: GigaCloud — Ukrainian cloud provider with PCI DSS certified infrastructure
why_relevant: Local cloud/hosting provider marketing PCI DSS-certified environments to fintechs and banks; a supply-side actor in the certification chain and a signal of where Ukrainian payment workloads are hosted.

source_name: PECB Ukraine — ISO/IEC 27001 certification and lead-auditor training body
why_relevant: Ukrainian arm of a management-system certification body; ISMS lead-auditor certificates from PECB/MSECB are one of the qualifications Держспецзв'язку accepts for attested information-security auditors, linking the training market to the attested-auditor population.

source_name: PSM7 (psm7.com) — Ukrainian payments trade media, processing-centre and certification coverage
why_relevant: Specialist payments outlet that publishes overviews of Ukrainian processing centres and their certifications; a snowballing hub for actor names, certification announcements and partnership news in the payments assurance layer.

source_name: Кібербез (cybersec.net.ua) — Ukrainian cybersecurity news, regulator document tracking
why_relevant: Tracks NBU and Держспецзв'язку draft regulations and cyber incidents affecting the banking system; useful early-warning layer and a pointer to primary regulator documents that name control and supplier requirements.

source_name: Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine — Прес-центр (official press centre)
why_relevant: Largest foreign-owned bank in Ukraine; its own press centre is the primary disclosure channel for platform go-lives, digital transformation milestones and named technology partners (e.g. the HR&Payroll / employee e-cabinet rollout for 6000 staff reported Dec 2025). Private bank, so no Prozorro trail.

source_name: OTP Bank Ukraine — News (English newsroom)
why_relevant: OTP Ukraine publishes technology-development items ('OTP Demo Day' technology/AI/personalisation updates) and named commercial partnerships. English mirror is machine-readable and paginated (~109 items observed), useful for vendor-name extraction.

source_name: OTP Bank Ukraine — Новини (Ukrainian newsroom)
why_relevant: Ukrainian-language edition typically carries items the English mirror omits or delays; local wording (впровадив, партнер, платформа) is the reliable trigger for vendor-selection detection.

source_name: OTP Group (Hungary) global newsroom / vendor announcements about OTP
why_relevant: Group-level vendor selections (Intellect Design Arena eMACH.ai digital core & lending, contract Dec 2023; Iliad Solutions t3 payments testing platform, 2024) cascade into the Ukrainian subsidiary. Vendor press releases name the deal the bank itself may not announce locally.
